name: Adaptive High-k DD32 Spectral Convergence Extension
interpretation: Every dataset is evaluated at k_max=24 and 32. Only unresolved datasets continue to 48 and then 64.

A convergence stop requires measured-tail contraction and quasi-monotonicity, <=3% last relative growth step, stable P2 verdict, no threshold overlap under the diagnostic extrapolation uncertainty proxy, a surviving k_max basis, <=10% exact k_max boundary weight, and decay of the highest-quarter Kelvin-mode energy.
The high-k tail gate is waived only when the entire Kelvin-family weight of the dominant eigenvector is below 5%, because high-k Kelvin truncation then cannot control the mode.
The g(k_max)=g_inf+c*k_max^{-p} fit is diagnostic only and cannot establish convergence by itself.
A geometry still unresolved at k_max=64 is reported as SPECTRAL_UNRESOLVED_AT_K64, not coerced into a PASS/FAIL convergence claim.
All rungs are linear-only and retain epsilon_ref=0.004; nonlinear ringdown/RPO/Floquet is intentionally not repeated at every high-k rung.
Convergence is refused when requested k_max exceeds 75% of the least-sampled component Nyquist limit.
